generatedBy: scripts/make-landscape.py from the zoom-19 satellite mosaic (not in the repository) - do not edit by hand
frame: x east, z south, metres; origin = centre of the running track (same frame as src/campus-data.js)
caveats: Everything here comes from ONE oblique satellite image; positions are good to a few metres at best.
The image is older than the new teaching building: an earlier building stands on its site, so nothing near it (z < -190 m) is reliable.
surveyArea is only the area in which ground cover was classified. It is not a surveyed campus boundary.

newBuildingSite.note: The new teaching building is newer than the mosaic and its builder lays out its own plaza and garden (2022 footage) around its own re-read footprint. No tree is placed in these zones; the ground there is plain lawn (garden zone) and plain paving (plaza zone and footprint grown 8 m) for the builder to draw on.

fields: crownRadius (trimmed where a building is closer than the crown seen)
trees.method: Canopy = pixels with (g-r >= 8 and brightness <= 78) or olive rough pixels (g-r 1..7, g-b >= 18, brightness 45..105, texture >= 9), on a 1 m grid (cell is canopy when half its pixels are). Trees are placed greedily at the cells deepest inside the canopy (3-4 chamfer distance), crown radius = that depth capped at 5.5 m, neighbours at least 0.8 x (r1 + r2) apart. Height 6..12 m in proportion to crown radius, +-0.5 m. The trunk is the crown centre moved back by the lean of the oblique view for a point at 0.7 x height (0.24 px west and 2.00 px north per metre), with +-0.8 m of jitter.
trees.trunksMovedNote: A trunk that landed up to 2.5 m inside a road edge, up to 4 m inside the edge of the courts block or over the edge of the canal belongs to a row standing along that edge (the crown overhangs it): it was put 1 m outside the edge instead of being dropped. Trunks deeper inside were dropped.
trees.droppedByCap: 21 trees: 21 outside the surveyed area, the ones farthest from it (more than 87 m from its edge)

ground.method: Per 1 m cell: paving = at least half the pixels bright (max channel >= 100) and not green (g-r <= 6); lawn = at least 55 % of the pixels green (g-r >= 8) and bright (79..175). ASSUMED: ground under tree crowns is planted (lawn); canal banks are lawn. Cells showing buildings, shadow or dark surfaces take the class of the nearest classified cell. 3 x 3 majority filter twice, specks under 20 m2 removed, outlines by marching squares on the grid smoothed over about 1.2 m, simplified to 0.3 m (the lawn outline is taken about 0.4 m wider so that it runs under the edge of the paving and no bare gap shows). Roads are drawn on top of whatever lies beside them. Roofs of buildings that are not in campus-data.js come out as paving.

canal.method: Water found on 92 image rows (every 25 px from y 460 to the bottom edge) as the longest smooth green run; west edge fitted by a straight line x = 1980.8 -0.1642 * y px (rms 3.7 px over 75 rows). The east edge is hidden by tree crowns and their shadow, so the banks are drawn parallel at the mean detected width (80 px; a separate fit of the east edge has rms 8.0 px). North of y 460 (z < -294 m) the canal passes under a road bridge and is extrapolated.
canal.confidence: seen in satellite and in the 2018 footage (frames 2-5): walled channel, tree rows on both banks. Water level and wall height not measured.

tennisCourts.confidence: seen in satellite only; single reading, +-1.5 m; whether they belong to the school is not confirmed

backdrop.note: Rough positions off a 0.4x overview (+-15 m or worse), generic sizes. Towers: [x, z, height]; sheds: [x1, z1, x2, z2, width, height].
